findings.where: Motion sketch, the 'Replay the entrance' control below the timing table (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: This control is a button: it replays the animation where it sits. But it looks exactly like the page's links, in link blue with an underline, which the page saves for navigation (the address and the PDF title). A visitor expects it to take them somewhere, not to act in place.
findings.who_objects: The founder trying the motion sketch: they cannot tell from its look whether clicking will leave the sheet or replay the line. If this look carries into the built site, it teaches visitors that blue underlined text sometimes doesn't go anywhere.

findings.where: First screen nav (Profile, Articles, Blog) and the article specimen's Download link ('Streamlining the PPP Process…')
findings.fault: These are dead links. The nav items point to #profile, #articles and #blog, but none of those sections exists on the page. The PDF title, set as a download, points to '#' and does nothing. All of them look like working links.
findings.who_objects: The founder clicking through the tile as a visitor would: the nav does nothing, and the download (the 'product' the research says follows the first look) doesn't download, so they can't judge how the reading and download path behaves.
